A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same V2X-R dataset, fusion pipeline, and MDD method. Their main sections, equations, and experiments can be matched reliably. v1 refers to supplementary material without including it; v3 includes supplementary Sections 7–12, assessed here as newly available reporting.

before.justification: v1 reports original V2X-R detection benchmarks, simulated-weather experiments, K-Radar evaluations, and MDD ablations in Section 5 and Tables 2–8.

after.justification: v3 retains original detection experiments and ablations and additionally reports detailed K-Radar weather results and qualitative point-cloud comparisons in its supplementary material.

M1.justification: The four-stage fusion pipeline, SA2MA and SM2MM adaptations, radar-conditioned U-Net denoising, diffusion procedure, and epoch-dependent loss remain unchanged. Supplementary Section 11 documents MDD implementation settings without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate detection on V2X-R and K-Radar with the same represented weather conditions and classes. v3 adds VoD point clouds for a qualitative comparison of real and simulated sensor data in Section 12 and Figure 6; it does not report a VoD detector benchmark.

E2.justification: v3 removes Where2comm's LiDAR-only, fusion, and fusion-with-MDD variants from the weather comparison in Table 5, although Where2comm remains in Tables 2–4. Table 6 relabels the unchanged K-Radar results from PointPillars to AttFuse with agent fusion removed; this does not establish a new underlying baseline experiment.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 revises the stated per-frame population from 2–7 CAVs to 2–5 agents. v3 also adds BEV AP evaluation on K-Radar alongside 3D AP. Existing V2X-R split counts, evaluation range, communication range, and normal/fog training with unseen-snow testing remain unchanged. These disclosures do not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds class-by-weather analysis of MDD's benefits and failures on K-Radar and a qualitative simulation-realism comparison using VoD. The component and diffusion-step/loss-weight ablations in Tables 7–8 are unchanged. Removing Where2comm from Table 5 reduces the architecture coverage of the weather-robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, variability across runs, or significance tests. The added supplementary results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Several benchmark results are replaced: Where2comm's testing 3D mAP at IoU 0.7 changes from 80.5 to 69.2 in Table 2 and from 56.7 to 41.5 in Table 3, changing the radar-only winner at that threshold to AdaFusion. SCOPE and CoBEVT entries also change, including CoBEVT's fusion validation scores in Table 4. v3 removes Where2comm's weather results and adds detailed K-Radar AP3D/APBEV results in Table 13; Tables 6–8 retain their numerical results. The revised agent statement and unexplained updates prevent interpreting the changed scores as established same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 and Algorithm 1 retain the same mathematical content. Explicitly identifying the final denoised feature as F0 in v3's prose restates the existing algorithm. No new proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first simulated V2X dataset incorporating LiDAR, cameras, and 4D radar, a cooperative fusion pipeline, and weather-robust MDD with the same headline improvement claims. v3 emphasizes the already-described reparameterization mechanism in its introduction without changing the contributions' scientific scope.

C2.justification: New Section 10.2 attributes Bus-class weather-dependent gains and losses to larger bounding boxes being sensitive to denoising; this is an explanatory assertion without a dedicated causal test. Section 12 adds an interpretation of simulation realism from visual comparisons. Meanwhile, v3 removes v1's explicit simulation-to-real gap qualification from the K-Radar discussion. The general limitation concerning deeper cooperative fusion remains.

D1.justification: v3 supplies substantial details deferred to absent supplementary material in v1: sensor coordinate conventions, data formats, sequence-to-split assignments, model-specific training budgets and learning rates, weather simulation parameters, K-Radar splits/labels/metrics, and U-Net/diffusion settings in Sections 7–11 and Tables 9–14. These mainly expand documentation rather than demonstrate implementation changes. v3 also promises training profiles and pretrained models; the shared dataset/code release remains described as forthcoming.

R1.justification: v3 adds the View-of-Delft paper by Palffy and colleagues to support the real-versus-simulated point-cloud comparison. The previously cited works and the main related-work positioning are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized rewrites to the abstract, introduction, methodological overview, and conclusion, and expands the introductory explanation of reparameterization. It also revises the title wording, author/affiliation block, and conclusion heading. The main section order and most prose remain intact, with supplementary sections appended.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the visual documentation through Tables 9–14, covering dataset metadata, configurations, and weather-specific results, plus Figure 6's multirow real/simulated point-cloud comparison. Figures 1 and 5 are revised, and Table 5 is shortened by removing the Where2comm block. The main pipeline figure and existing performance plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The supplementary material makes the dataset and experiments substantially easier to audit through previously missing configurations, data conventions, and weather-specific outcomes, including cases where MDD hurts performance. These transparency gains outweigh the narrower weather comparison. However, the removed Where2comm evidence and unexplained benchmark-score and agent-setting revisions limit the net improvement and leave their relationship to the original experiments unresolved.
